$comment: HAND-EDITED source of the Agent Messages settings: how a message from another agent or a person (cmux agent message) reaches an agent in a terminal (issue 36496). The daemon applies these keys' effective values (its settings owner's merge, managed layers included) in agent.message.wait (cmux-tui/crates/cmux-tui-core/src/mux/agent_message_wait.rs) and checks this file's defaults in its tests; gen-settings-sources.py writes the Swift descriptors and parser constants. Row fields: see schemas/settings/source/updates.json.

lists.name: agentMessages
lists.note: Settings > Agents > Agent Messages (issue 36496). Messages always reach an agent in its turns (the prompt hook); this decides whether an idle one is woken for them.

rows.name: claudeWake
rows.note: On: Claude Code in a cmux terminal, started through cmux's claude wrapper, runs a background asyncRewake hook after its start and each turn that waits in the daemon (agent.message.wait) and wakes an idle session with its messages as a system reminder. Off (the effective value, so an MDM or team value that forces it off wins): the daemon answers the wake hook's wait disabled and the hook exits; messages wait for the session's next prompt. A change wakes waiting hooks to recheck; turned on again, the wake re-arms at Claude's next start or turn end.

help.text: When another agent or a person sends a message to Claude Code in a terminal, an idle session starts a turn to read it. Nothing is typed into the terminal. Off: the message waits for the next prompt in that session.
